content.title: About
content.content: Sesame butter, creamy is a paste made from ground roasted sesame seeds, featuring a smooth, buttery flavor and velvety texture. It is a staple in Middle Eastern cuisine, used in sauces, desserts, and as a spread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sesame is one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 5,000 years.
Tahini is the base of the classic hummus dip.
In some cultures tahini is served with sweet dishes such as pancakes and honey.
Sesame seeds are rich in lignans, which may influence hormonal balance.
Tahini is frequently used in vegan cooking as an egg substitute.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Sesame provides more calcium than most nuts and seeds, supporting bone health.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Tahini contains monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: High in vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides plant protein
items.content: Tahini supplies plant‑based protein, valuable for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: Sesame allergy
items.content: Sesame is a major allergen; reactions can be severe.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Tahini is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Sesame contains oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use tahini as a spread on bread, blend into smoothies, add to sauces, marinades, desserts, or baked goods. Mixing with water or lemon juice creates a thinner consistency for dressings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store tahini in an airtight jar in a cool, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it refrigerated to prevent fat oxidation.
